picks.why: 16.5x trailing with EPS still growing, and Q3 showed streaming profitable and parks at a record, so this is a sound franchise at a discount with no report due until November.

17.8x trailing for a cash-rich franchise whose Cloud business grew 82% and whose shares are down 10.7% over 12 weeks; even if part of the 112% EPS jump is non-operating, that is a low price for this business.

12.2x trailing on EPS up 89% is a low multiple for the biggest gold producer, and the weak dollar is behind gold; I'll own it while it holds the Council's $105 line and accept that it swings more than the rest of the book.
11.4x trailing with EPS up 10% makes the best underwriter in auto insurance the cheapest financial on the list, and it depends less on how CPI comes in than anything else I own.

16.4x for the best-run money-center bank with EPS up 13%, it is one of the two steadiest stocks on the list, and it has cleared the $355 line I was waiting for while the steeper curve helps its lending margins.

summary: A cheap-and-sound book: trailing P/E averages about 14.9, EPS is growing at all five, and the picks span four sectors instead of resting on one macro bet ahead of Tuesday's CPI. I passed on ALB (21.9x trailing and still down 27% over 12 weeks despite the Q2 beat), HON (its trailing figures span its breakup) and the low-multiple STZ, CALM, SM and VICI, whose earnings are shrinking. I used nothing from memory about how this week went; the picks rest on the two files alone.
